summary: Deprecates the RC4 stream cipher in Secure Shell and, as a result, moves RFC 4345 to Historic status. It is a best-practice document recommending that SSH implementations stop using RC4 because of its weaknesses.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8758 says SSH must not use RC4 ciphers because they have known weaknesses. It also updates the relevant SSH cipher registry entries.

questions: should rc4 be used in ssh
why was rc4 deprecated in ssh
which ssh cipher names are marked historic
subtitle: A best current practice prohibiting RC4 ciphers in SSH.

tldr.problem: RC4 ciphers used in SSH have known weaknesses.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC updates RFC 4253 to change arcfour from OPTIONAL to MUST NOT, moves RFC 4345 to Historic, and marks three RC4 cipher names HISTORIC in the IANA registry.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8758 updates RFC 4253 and is a Best Current Practice. The unit metadata lists it as updating RFC 4253.

today: RFC 8758 is a Best Current Practice and updates RFC 4253, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Why RC4 Is Deprecated
sections.content: RFC 4253 and RFC 4345 specify RC4 suites for Secure Shell (SSH), also called arcfour. The RFC states that RC4 has known weaknesses and starts the deprecation of its use in SSH. It also moves RFC 4345 to Historic because all ciphers it specifies must not be used.
sections.plainLanguage: RC4, also called arcfour, has known weaknesses. This RFC begins its removal from SSH.

sections.title: The SSH Cipher Rule
sections.content: RFC 4253 listed the arcfour cipher as OPTIONAL. RFC 8758 changes that status to MUST NOT and updates the accompanying text to state that arcfour and RC4 have known weaknesses and MUST NOT be used. The RFC also moves RFC 4345, which specifies arcfour128 and arcfour256, to Historic status.
sections.plainLanguage: The SSH rule changes from allowing arcfour to prohibiting it. The RFC that specified two related variants is moved to Historic.

sections.title: IANA Registry Updates
sections.content: IANA updated the SSH Encryption Algorithm Names subregistry. It marks arcfour, arcfour128, and arcfour256 as HISTORIC. The RFC says it only prohibits RC4 in SSH and introduces no new security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The official SSH algorithm list marks all three RC4 names as Historic. The RFC says the prohibition adds no new security considerations.
